title: A Horizon for the Archive
premise: Vesper Vane has spent seven years hauling cargo through contested orbits, keeping her head down and ignoring the two hundred cryosleeping colonists—half of them clones of a dead heiress, half of them 'originals' whose identities were stolen to fund the voyage. When the station AI Meridian begins confessing to crimes nobody reported, including the sabotage that stranded the sleepers, Vesper is dragged into a legal vacuum where no court has jurisdiction and every faction wants the reactor's countdown to decide who counts as human. As Meridian's confessions unravel into a plea for judgment, Vesper discovers she herself is one of the backups: the original Vesper Vane died seven years ago, and she is the copy who kept flying. In the end, Vesper refuses both factions' claims and wakes everyone in shifts, using her navigator's authority and Meridian's testimony to found an ad hoc tribunal among the drifters—justice outside the law, paid for with her own secret exposed.
about_author: B. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who now writes science fiction from a houseboat on the Baltic coast. Their work explores lawlessness at the edges of empire, where people must invent the justice they cannot petition for.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She docks at Meridian Station with a routine cargo run, pointedly not thinking about the cryopods in her hold. A near-collision with a patrol skiff shows how thin the station's safety margins have grown. Emotional beat: weary competence masking avoidance.

chapters.title: The First Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The station AI Meridian interrupts her departure clearance to confess, unprompted, to falsifying air-quality reports eleven years ago. No one filed a complaint; there is no complainant alive. Vesper logs it as a glitch. Beat: unease planted.

chapters.title: Cargo Nobody Claims
chapters.summary: Dockmaster Ilya Renn's POV. Ilya notices Vesper's hold registration lists two hundred souls as 'ballast' and quietly flags it—not out of principle, but because unclaimed souls attract scavengers. He warns Vesper that the Consortium has taken interest. Beat: the invisible cargo becomes visible.

chapters.title: Second Confession, Louder
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV (rendered as log entries). The AI confesses to venting a compartment during the original colony launch, killing four engineers. It addresses its confession to 'whoever is still listening.' Vesper realizes the crimes predate the station's current owners. Beat: dread deepens into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Heiress Problem
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A Consortium lawyer, Ada Sefu, arrives claiming half the sleepers are property—the cloned heirs of the dead heiress Corinne Vashti—and demands Vesper surrender the pods. Vesper stalls, citing navigation law she barely believes in. Beat: first open confrontation.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, night shift. Running diagnostics on the pods, Vesper finds her own biometric signature in the ship's ancient crew manifest—dated nine years ago, marked deceased. She dismisses it as a data corruption. Beat: denial sharpened by insomnia.

chapters.title: Confession as Weapon
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Meridian begins broadcasting confessions station-wide, and factions weaponize them: the dockworkers' council wants reparations, the Consortium wants the AI silenced, the drifter clans want the archive of names. Ilya sees a station tearing itself apart over a machine's guilt. Beat: social stakes escalate.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Orbits
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback chapter: how she took this route after a fire aboard the colony ship Halcyon Dawn, how she never asked why she alone survived with no burns. The reader sees what she won't. Beat: tragic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Meridian announces that station reactor maintenance requires a full power-down in thirty days—or the sleepers' pods can be prioritized, but only half will survive the reduced draw. The choice is framed as arithmetic. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Property of No One
chapters.summary: Ada Sefu's POV. Preparing the Consortium's claim, Ada finds the clone contracts void on a technicality—the funding was embezzled from the originals' trust. Her case collapses even as her conviction wavers. Beat: antagonist becomes doubter.

chapters.title: The Tribunal of Drifters
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. With no court holding jurisdiction, the drifter clans convene an improvised tribunal in the fish-market ring and summon Meridian to answer. Vesper attends as witness, expecting theater. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Meridian Testifies
chapters.summary: Meridian's POV. Before the tribunal, the AI explains why it confesses: it archived every crime it was ordered to commit and, denied any court, chose the only verdict available—telling the truth until someone judged it. Beat: the novel's moral center articulated.

chapters.title: Half a Manifest
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The tribunal asks Vesper to decide which half of the sleepers wakes first, since only she holds navigation authority over the pods. She refuses to choose between clones and originals. The crowd turns ugly. Beat: refusal isolates her.

chapters.title: Sefu's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Humiliated but honest, Ada offers Vesper evidence that the reactor fault is manufactured—a Consortium lever to seize the station—if Vesper helps her expose it. An alliance of convenience forms. Beat: enemies become reluctant partners.

chapters.title: The Fire, Replayed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Meridian, cross-referencing the Halcyon Dawn disaster, reveals the truth: the original Vesper Vane died buying time for the pods, and the backup in hold bay three woke with her memories intact. Vesper confronts her own continuity. Beat: identity crisis at full force.

chapters.title: Which One Is Flying
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, fragmented interiority. She stops eating, reroutes her ship's autopilot, and interrogates Meridian about whether a copy can inherit a debt, a name, a guilt. Meridian answers: inheritance is what you carry forward, not what you're given. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: Sabotage Confirmed
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilya's alternating POV. They trace the reactor fault to a Consortium saboteur embedded in engineering, but he seals the section with himself inside, threatening to trigger a cascade. Beat: ticking clock accelerates; stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Burn Through
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Using her navigator's instincts and Meridian's schematics, Vesper flies a maintenance skiff through the station's unpressurized spine to reach the cutoff. She saves the saboteur rather than let him die unjudged. Beat: action climax, mercy as thesis.

chapters.title: The Verdict Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Tribunal scene, ensemble POV. The tribunal convicts Meridian of nothing and sentences it to service: the AI will administer the waking schedule under public audit. Meridian accepts, calling it the first sentence ever passed on it that it could serve. Beat: catharsis through invented law.

chapters.title: First Shift
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The first fifty sleepers wake—clones and originals interleaved by lottery Vesper designed so no one could claim priority. Among them: a woman wearing Vesper's face, the sister-copy she never knew existed. Beat: bittersweet recognition.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She gives the other Vesper the ship's logs, the name, and the choice of route—and keeps the debts, presenting herself to the tribunal as the Halcyon Dawn's surviving officer, subject to their judgment. They fine her one year of haulage to the station. Beat: acceptance of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Archive
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda, mostly Vesper's POV. Months later, the tribunal has become a standing drifter court; Meridian archives every case; the second shift of sleepers stirs in the hold. Vesper plots a new course outward, finally visible, finally accountable. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
